The Fifthism and Church of the Second Hytoth tests should be switched in order, imo. Right now, there are three tests where the water is transmuted into blood. Two of them are next to each other (Sarkicism and Scarlet King), but there's another test separating those two from the third (Second Hytoth). item.content:encoded:
I'm not in agreement with this. The Foundation isn't just a prison, it's an enormous science lab. Their goal is to create that structure that understands the anomalies - else, why both running tests and experiments? Why bother exploring? Why do anything other than lock the anomalies away under lock and key? Heck, why not just destroy as many as possible? Containment achieves nothing that destruction doesn't achieve better when it comes to security.

It's because the essence of the Foundation has never just been containment. It's also been testing, experimenting, exploring, and learning. From learning comes understanding. From understanding can come entire branches of study, new science, new technology. Advancing enough that you can quantitatively measure certain things that couldn't be measured before isn't a cop-out, it's exactly what the Foundation, if it is at all effective in its efforts, SHOULD be getting to.

As for releasing it…well, they can't release that without also bringing awareness to a whole bunch of things that might cause a whole hell of a lot of trouble. Any brand-new science brings paradigm shifts, which can cause as much bad as good - and given the Foundation deals with a lot of things that will Kill You Right Dead Or Worse, it's probably not something they want to throw out there haphazardly.

item.content:encoded:
There are several things that have been bothering me ever since I first read this.

Issues
- Close

-The Fifthism test doesn't make sense. In all articles, Fifthism places great significance on smoke and little, if any, on the materials used to produce the smoke. SCP-1523 even states that the anomaly isn't the incense coil but is in fact the smoke itself, so the connection to it implies (to me at least) you misread or misunderstood the article. And after the Cogwork Orthodox test I assumed you were going to use the transformations described in SCP-1564.

-"Local reality changes and an increase in a subjects faith" seems accurate to the first four tests but a significant understatement of the others. It seems to me you have most of the para-religious subjects become something highly regarded in their faith, which also seems uneven between them. Becoming a robot like your god or turning into the god of your own little universe is significantly different to getting a religious symbol on your forehead or markings on your hands. It would make more sense for the three christian subjects to ascend to heaven or for the ortothan to lose all their blood if the other changes are going to be so extreme.

Less important comments/questions
- Close

-I really like the memoir.

-I like the idea of Site-36 being a research base for religious anomalies.

-I was wondering why you consider SCP-001 to be related to The Radiant Father? Given that myths and records of him and his cult date really far back and theres no evidence of SCP-001-A existing pre-history, it seems unlikely to me that he would be the reason for SCP-001. To be clear I'm not trying to change your mind, I'm just curious about your headcanon. I always considered either SCP-1682, Fifthism, or some freak anomaly to be the reason for SCP-001.
